title: MCP — Overview
description: Golden signals for an AskTurret MCP deployment: request rate, error rate, and latency. Every expression is checked against the emitted metric set by .github/scripts/check-dashboard-metrics.mjs, so a panel here cannot silently outlive the metric it queries.

panels.title: Request rate by method
panels.description: MCP protocol requests per second. A flat line at zero here while pods are up usually means the scrape is broken, not that traffic stopped.

panels.title: Error ratio
panels.description: Fraction of requests whose outcome is `error`. This is the SLO signal: the reference target is 99.9% of tools/call returning a TYPED result within deadline, so sustained values above 0.001 are burning budget.

panels.title: Tool call latency (p50 / p95 / p99)
panels.description: Per-tool duration quantiles. Read p99 against the deadline you configured — a p99 that sits just under it is a deployment one slow upstream away from shedding calls.

panels.title: Tool call rate by tool and outcome
panels.description: Which tools are actually used. A tool with no traffic is either dead configuration or an agent that never discovered it — both worth knowing before an upgrade.

panels.title: Errors by code
panels.description: Broken down by typed error code rather than by count alone — a rise in UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE and a rise in POLICY_DENIED need opposite responses.

panels.title: In-flight calls by tool
panels.description: Concurrency actually observed per tool. Compare against the bulkhead limits on the Reliability dashboard: in-flight pinned at the limit is saturation, not throughput.

panels.title: Request duration p99 by method
panels.description: End-to-end protocol latency, which includes policy evaluation and serialization — so it can diverge from tool latency when policy is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Response size p99 by tool
panels.description: Serialized output bytes. A tool trending toward the configured response-size limit will start returning OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE before it returns anything wrong, so this is the earlier signal.
